description:
PearList keeps your household's shared lists in sync across everyone's phones, with no account, no server and no company in the middle.

Make a grocery list, a to-do list or a chore board. Anyone in your household can add items, check them off, rename them, assign them and delete them, and every change syncs directly between your phones. Assign an item to a person and any list doubles as a shared chore board.

There is no sign-up and no login. You join a household by scanning a QR code or tapping an invite link. From then on everyone sees and edits the same lists.
  
Because PearList is peer-to-peer, your lists live only on your devices. They are never uploaded to a server, so no company can read them, sell them or lose them in a breach. Everything syncs encrypted, directly device to device.

Features
 - Multiple shared lists per household: groceries, to-dos, chores
 - Add, check, rename, assign and delete items, synced to everyone
 - Assign items to a person to use any list as a chore board
 - Join by QR code or invite link, no account needed
 - Works offline, syncs when your devices are online together
 - Open source and private by design: no account, no ads, no tracking

PearList is fully open source: https://github.com/peerloomllc/pearlist
promotionalText: Shared household lists that sync directly between your phones. No account, no server, no tracking. Groceries, to-dos and chores, private by design.
whatsNew:
## What's Changed

### Saved lists

Shopping for the same things every week? Save a list and start a fresh copy of it whenever you like, instead of typing it out again.

Open a list, tap its options and choose "Save as template". After that, "Start from a saved list" appears above where you add lists. The new list arrives with everything unticked and each item already in the right aisle.

Saved lists stay on your own phone, so nothing about them reaches anyone else in your household until you start one.

### Connect Anywhere

Your phones normally talk straight to each other, but some mobile networks block that, and until now a list you changed while out could sit unsynced until you got home.

PearList can now fall back to a PeerLoom relay that passes the scrambled data along, so your lists keep syncing wherever you are. The relay cannot read your lists. It only sees that two devices are talking and how much data went by, and it keeps nothing.

It is on by default, and there is a switch in Settings if you would rather stay strictly phone to phone. Underneath it, a line tells you whether it has actually been needed.

### Better aisle sorting

Your groceries sort themselves into store aisles as you add them, and this release makes that a lot more reliable. We added 346 more brand names and fixed a batch of everyday items that were landing somewhere silly: potato chips and apple juice were going to Produce, chicken broth to Meat, hand soap and shaving cream to the wrong aisle entirely.

Sorting happens the instant you type an item, with nothing to download and nothing to wait for. If something still lands in the wrong place, drag it where it belongs and PearList remembers your choice for next time.

### Local AI has been removed

PearList used to offer an optional "Local AI" that ran a small language model on your phone to guess the aisle for items it did not know, and to turn a pasted recipe into a shopping list. We have taken it out.

We would rather tell you why than quietly drop it. We tested it properly and it simply was not good enough: it picked the right aisle well under half the time, took several seconds for every single item, and needed a 0.8 GB download to do it. The instant sorting described above turned out to be both faster and more accurate without it.

If you had Local AI switched on, that 0.8 GB is deleted for you automatically the next time you open PearList. There is nothing for you to do, and you get the space back.

### A much smaller app

Between that and some other trimming, PearList is a lot lighter than it was: much less to download and much less room taken up on your phone.
